issues.description: Default response transformer crashes on any non-JSON line; unhandled JSONDecodeError aborts the stream and strands bookend state
issues.detail: default_response_to_output_transformer calls json.loads(response_line) with no try/except. A single malformed SSE line (keep-alive, partial chunk, transport hiccup, error payload) raises JSONDecodeError out of process_frame, aborting the entire turn and leaving _output_response_open=True with a dangling _close_task. Either catch and log+skip, or state and enforce the precondition that lines are well-formed JSON. Also wrap the invoke loop in try/finally so bookends always close on exception or cancellation.

issues.description: AWS client created per inbound context frame instead of reused across the processor lifetime
issues.detail: Every LLMContextFrame opens a fresh aioboto3 client via `async with self._aws_session.client('bedrock-agentcore', ...)`. This pays TCP/TLS handshake, credential resolution, and signing setup on every turn, adding nontrivial latency in a streaming voice pipeline. The client is a long-lived identity that should be created once (lazily on first use or in a startup/setup hook) and torn down on cleanup. Per-invocation construction conflates session lifetime with request lifetime.

issues.description: Public `agentArn` parameter violates snake_case convention used throughout the module and codebase
issues.detail: Every other constructor parameter is snake_case (aws_access_key, aws_region, aws_session_token, context_to_payload_transformer). `agentArn` is camelCase, presumably mirroring the AWS API field `agentRuntimeArn`. AWS wire naming is an implementation detail; the Python-facing identity should be `agent_arn` (with the internal attribute renamed accordingly) and translated to `agentRuntimeArn` only at the boto3 boundary. Renaming a public kwarg later is a breaking change, so fix before shipping.

issues.description: Output-response bookend state machine is racy and the 1.0s timeout is redundant with stream-end signals
issues.detail: The processor maintains _output_response_open, _close_task, and _last_text_frame_time to bracket LLMFullResponseStart/End frames, but the invariant (Start frames equal End frames in order) is not preserved under concurrent or re-entrant invocations: two interleaved context frames can produce Start/Start/End or text frames after End. The 1.0s timeout-close runs in parallel with the explicit post-loop close, creating a second mechanism doing the same job. process_frame already knows exactly when the stream ends (the line after the async-for loop). Drop the timer, emit Start before the loop iff any text was produced and End after, and either serialize context-frame handling or scope the bookend state per-invocation.

issues.description: Hand-rolled SSE parsing is incorrect for multi-line data, CRLF, comments, and chunk-boundary splits
issues.detail: The multi-part branch splits on `\n`, hardcodes a 6-char `data: ` prefix slice, warns on anything else, and drops valid SSE features (multi-line `data:` continuations terminated by blank lines, `event:`/`id:`/`retry:` fields, `:` comment lines, CRLF endings). It also assumes chunk boundaries align with line boundaries, which the protocol does not guarantee — a mid-line chunk split silently corrupts parsing. Use a real SSE parser or factor a small `iter_sse_data(part_bytes)` generator with a stated contract, shared by both single-part and multi-part branches, and replace the magic `6` with `len('data: ')` or `removeprefix`.

issues.description: Star-import with no `__all__` leaks helpers and transitive imports into the package public API
issues.detail: agent_core.py defines no `__all__`, so `from .agent_core import *` in the package `__init__.py` re-exports `asyncio`, `json`, `os`, `aioboto3`, `logger`, every imported Frame type, plus the two default transformers — making the public surface accidentally large and fragile. Either define `__all__ = ['AWSAgentCoreProcessor', 'default_context_to_payload_transformer', 'default_response_to_output_transformer']` or import the names explicitly in `__init__.py`.

issues.description: Credentials snapshotted from os.environ at __init__ time, breaking rotation and refresh
issues.detail: The constructor reads AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID, AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY, AWS_SESSION_TOKEN, and AWS_REGION via os.getenv at construction and freezes them into _aws_params. STS-issued temporary credentials expire mid-session; instance/role, container, and SSO refresh providers are bypassed because explicit None/string values override boto3's credential chain. The aws_session_token docstring also doesn't disclose the env fallback, so callers passing None silently get an environment token. Let aioboto3 resolve credentials itself when the caller doesn't pass them, or document the restriction loudly.

issues.description: Dead state: `_last_text_frame_time` is written but never read
issues.detail: _last_text_frame_time is assigned in _push_text_frame but never consumed anywhere — the close-after-timeout logic only checks _output_response_open. Either delete the field or use it (e.g., a single idle-timer task that loops on this timestamp instead of cancel/recreate). Also prefer `asyncio.get_running_loop()` over the deprecated `asyncio.get_event_loop()`.

issues.description: Class name, module docstring, and PR title disagree
issues.detail: The module docstring references `AWSAgentCoreProcessor`, the PR title says `AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor`, and the class is `AWSAgentCoreProcessor`. Pick one name (the more searchable `AWSBedrockAgentCoreProcessor` aligns with the AWS product naming) and align class, module docstring, and PR title.

`" ".join([part.get('text', '') for part in content])` assumes every list element is a dict with `.get`, will raise AttributeError on non-dict parts, and silently produces empty strings (and stray spaces) for image/tool_use/audio parts. The postcondition is not stated. Filter to `isinstance(part, dict) and part.get('type') == 'text'`, or document loudly that the default transformer is text-only and multimodal callers must supply their own.

issues.description: Magic constants for SSE prefix length and response timeout
issues.detail: `line[6:]` hardcodes the length of `data: ` in two places. `_output_response_timeout = 1.0` is hardcoded inside __init__ with no comment, no constructor parameter, and no justification — and 1.0s is a long time in a voice pipeline where end-of-response latency affects perceived turn-taking. Replace the slice with `removeprefix('data: ')` or a named constant, and expose the timeout as a constructor parameter (or remove it if the bookend rework above eliminates the need).

issues.description: No unit tests for the two pure transformer functions or the bookend logic
issues.detail: `default_context_to_payload_transformer` and `default_response_to_output_transformer` are pure string-in/string-out functions and are trivial to test, but the diff ships with none. The processor's timeout/close logic is exactly the kind of stateful code that grows silent bugs in production. At minimum, land unit tests for the two transformers and cover the happy path plus the timeout/race for the bookend state.

synthesis.summary: The panel converges on a NEEDS-WORK verdict: the core shape (context-in, AgentCore invoke, SSE parts out, text frames downstream) is reasonable, but the implementation has not been reasoned through. Three issues are unanimous P0-class: the default response transformer crashes on any non-JSON line and leaves bookend state stranded; the AWS client is constructed per inbound frame, paying TLS/credential-resolution cost on every turn; and the public `agentArn` parameter violates the codebase's snake_case convention and must be renamed before shipping as a stable API. The streaming machinery layers a redundant 1.0s wall-clock timeout on top of signals the async iterator already provides, creating a race against the explicit post-loop close, and the hand-rolled SSE parser silently drops valid-per-spec lines and assumes chunk boundaries align with line boundaries. Smaller cleanups — `__all__`, env-frozen credentials, dead `_last_text_frame_time`, class/docstring/PR-title disagreement, magic constants, multimodal content handling, and missing unit tests — should land in the same pass.
